doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Transcribing Smithsonian interviews from CDs
summary: Rowe asks about his transcribing of Smithsonian interviews, which were on CD in the early 2000s.

story.theme_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: Okay. Well I’m going to wrap up here, this has been fascinating. One question I wanted to get in that’s very relevant to us, when we have our interviews my wife has done all these transcriptions. And I learned that you did a lot of transcribing of the Smithsonian interviews. And we were curious, the logistics of how did you do that? Were they on cassettes or were they reel to reel tapes?
No this was much later. This was all on CDs. This was like — I don’t remember exactly the years but after 2000. Early 21st century so it was all, it was very easy. It was all on CD.
